fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Detached Structure; Access Drive; Vehicle Parking Area; Open Lawn Area; Dense Vegetation; Walkway
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Limited Rear Access; Multiple Structures
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responders can identify the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the access drive entrance clearly on both sides to help responders locate the single entry point under low-visibility conditions.
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the access drive to allow emergency vehicles to pass without obstruction.
• Cut back dense vegetation near the detached structures so responders can reach and move around those buildings.
• Keep a clear path along at least one side of the main residence connecting the front to the rear of the property.
• Mark any rear gates or side access points so responders can locate them without searching.
• Keep rear gates unlocked or secured with a breakaway latch to allow responder access without delay.
• Clear a staging area near the parking zone large enough for emergency vehicles to park without blocking the access drive.
• Thin dense vegetation between structures so responders can move between buildings without pushing through heavy growth.
• Post a simple site map at the driveway entrance showing the location of all structures and any rear access limitations.

wildfire.conditions: Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Mixed Vegetation; Ground Vegetation; Tall Grass Area; Scattered Shrubs; Open Terrain; Limited Vegetation Separation; Single Access Route; Woody Debris; Adequate Vegetation Separation
wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin the tree cluster closest to the structure to create open space between the trees and the building.
• Remove dead branches and woody debris from the ground near the structure.
• Trim shrubs that are growing directly against or touching the structure.
• Separate tall grass areas from the structure by mowing or cutting grass back from the building's edges.
• Thin scattered trees near the structure so individual tree canopies are not touching each other.
• Cut or mow tall grass along the single access route to keep it clear for vehicles.
• Trim overhanging branches along the driveway so emergency vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Remove accumulated woody debris from beneath trees near the structure.
• Cut back mixed vegetation growing close to the structure's walls, foundation, and corners.
• Keep ground vegetation immediately around the structure short and sparse.
• Clear scattered shrubs that are growing beneath or near tree canopies close to the structure.
• Maintain the open terrain areas around the structure by preventing shrub or grass regrowth into those spaces.
• Mark the single access route clearly so it remains identifiable for emergency responders entering the property.
